Crow’s Feet: What Causes Them and What Really Helps

Crow’s feet are the fine lines that fan out from the outer corners of the eyes, and skincare can soften how they look but cannot stop the movement that makes them.

By the Skingenetix Research Team, medically reviewed by Dr Esther Bodde, 9 October 2026

subheading.en: Argireline: crow’s feet graded clearly smoother

content.en: After 4 weeks; none of 15 on placebo (Wang 2013).
After 28 days, against 6.6% on the retinol side; no placebo (Ye 2026).

subheading.en: GHK-Cu: more wrinkle-volume reduction than the plain serum base

content.en: Near the eye corner, after 8 weeks (Badenhorst 2016).

In short:

  • What causes them? Years of smiling and squinting fold the skin there, and sun exposure and lost elasticity set the folds in.
  • What helps? Daily sunscreen first. After that, a few ingredients have been tested on crow’s feet in controlled trials, with modest results, listed in the table below.
  • What does not exist? A cream that removes them.

Crow’s feet are one of the line types covered on our Fine Lines and Wrinkles page, and Argireline, the ingredient in the first trial below, has its own Argireline research page. Every number below comes from our appraisal of each trial, linked in the table.

Is it crow’s feet, crows’ feet or crows feet?

All three spellings point at the same thing. “Crow’s feet” is the usual written form, “crows’ feet” also appears, and “crows feet” is how many people type it into a search box. The name comes from the shape of the lines, which spread like a bird’s foot.

Doctors call them lateral canthal lines, meaning the lines at the outer corner of the eye. They are different from the lines under the eye, which have their own section below.

Why do crow’s feet show when you smile, and why do they stay?

Smiling, laughing and squinting tighten the ring of muscle around the eye and fold the skin at its outer edge. In young skin the folds spring back. These are the lines you see only when you smile.

Over the years, sun exposure and the gradual loss of skin elasticity make the skin slower to spring back. The folds then stay visible at rest. So there are two kinds of line: the one that appears with the expression, and the one that remains when your face is still.

The difference matters for creams. A cream works on the skin’s surface. It does not stop you smiling, and the trials below do not claim that it does.

At what age do crow’s feet appear?

There is no single age. It depends on how much your face moves, how much sun your skin has had, your skin type and your family. The trials below recruited adults aged 25 to 65, all with visible lines at the eye corner, so lines are common across that whole range.

Which skincare ingredients have been tested on crow’s feet?

We know of five controlled trials that measured the skin at the eye corner. Each is already appraised on our site. The table sets them side by side.

How do you choose a cream for crow’s feet?

Use the table as a checklist rather than a shopping list:

title.en: Look for an ingredient with a crow’s-feet trial

content.en: Many ingredients have no trial at the eye corner at all.

title.en: Check the label for the amount

content.en: A trial result belongs to the strength and formula tested. If a label gives no percentage, you cannot tell whether it matches anything studied.
Most of the five above were funded, run or supplied by a maker or seller of the ingredient. That does not make them wrong, but it is worth knowing.
It is the one step aimed at the cause rather than the look.

Our Acetyl Hexapeptide-8 Anti-Wrinkle Serum contains Argireline, the ingredient in the Wang trial. We have not tested the serum ourselves, so we cannot say it will give the same result. Our PDRN Renewal Serum contains PDRN, the ingredient in the Ye trial; that trial tested an eye cream, not this serum.

Can you get rid of crow’s feet naturally?

You can slow how fast they deepen, but no natural method removes lines that are already set. The steps that make a difference are the dull ones: sunscreen every morning, sunglasses on bright days so you squint less, and not smoking.

Be wary of any page that promises the lines will “disappear”. In the trials above, the best-measured change in crow’s-feet area was a 23.0% fall, which is softer lines, not no lines.

What do Koreans use for under-eye wrinkles?

People who ask this are often thinking of PDRN, a salmon-derived ingredient popular in Korean skincare. We have no trial of under-eye wrinkles run in Korea, so we will not call anything here Korean evidence.

The trial we do have is Ye 2026, which was run in China. It tested a 0.1% PDRN eye cream on 31 women, twice a day for 28 days, against 0.1% retinol on the other side of the face. The number of under-eye lines (a different measure from the crow’s-feet area in the table) fell 23.4% on the PDRN side against 7.0% on the retinol side, and eye-bag volume fell 14.8% against 10.2%. Both sides improved, there was no placebo side, and it describes the ingredient, not our products.

Under-eye lines have their own causes and need their own article. For now, read the full trial on the Ye 2026 study page.

What can a professional offer for crow’s feet?

A doctor or clinic can offer treatments such as botulinum toxin injections, fillers, laser, peels and light-based devices. We name them only so you know they exist.

They are different in kind from a cream. None of the trials above says anything about them, and a cream’s result does not transfer to them or the other way round. If you are weighing them up, ask a qualified practitioner what suits your skin, and ask to see evidence for the specific treatment.
Using actives near the eyes safely, and when to see someone

Try a small amount on the inner forearm or behind the ear for a day or two.

Keep products out of the eyes and off the edge of the lid.
None of these ingredients has been tested in those groups, so ask a doctor or pharmacist first.

title.en: Argireline is for the skin’s surface only

content.en: Never inject it, and never use it with a derma stamp or roller.
Do not use it on broken skin or if you are allergic to fish.
Do not use at the same time as pure vitamin C, strong acids or high-strength retinol. Use them at another time of day. No combination has been trialled.

See a doctor if you have a drooping eyelid, a lump near the eye, or lines that come with a rash.
